messages:
Riley (People Ops): Quick sync  we're seeing multiple requests for 'split-location months' where folks spend intermittent weeks abroad or in another US state. Need consensus on WFH stipend handling, payroll flags, and any short attestation.

Samir (Eng): I'm planning a 10-day work trip to Austin every month for the next 6 months to pair with a remote contractor. Do I still get full monthly stipend?

Tess (Finance): Short answer: stipend treatment depends on whether the company is paying coworking or it's a personal expense. If personal, we typically prorate when days away from homebase exceed a de minimis threshold. Also need travel pattern for withholding considerations.

Dana (Legal): Important: regular presence in another jurisdiction can create income tax withholding or employer nexus depending on activities (interviewing, contracting, sales). Even pairing with contractors may be a risk because it involves supervising third parties. Please disclose the exact nature of work performed onsite.

Riley (People Ops): Proposed interim policy: 1) For recurring short trips (<90 consecutive days), default = prorate monthly stipend by calendar days spent at homebase vs other location. 2) If coworking is invoiced to Redwood, no stipend duplication. 3) Manager+Finance can approve full stipend for business-justified patterns.

Samir (Eng): Example math? If I spend 10 out of 30 days in Austin, what do I expect?

Tess (Finance): We'll calculate (homebase_days/total_days) * stipend. If homebase_days=20 and stipend=$200, payout=$133. We round to nearest dollar. Any state tax withholdings will be noted on the paystub and may require you to file a nonresident return.

Riley (People Ops): Employee process: open People Ops case with dates, addresses, and whether you'll do interviews/hiring locally. Attach contractor details if interacting with contractors. We'll run a quick tax/nexus check and loop in Finance/Legal. Response target 3 business days.

PeopleOps-Bot: Case created #37210 "Samir - monthly Austin trip".

Samir (Eng): If I occasionally meet a candidate in person while there (1-2 interviews over six months), does that change anything?

Dana (Legal): Flag that to People Ops. One-off interviews are usually low risk but repeated recruiting activities increase the chance of nexus. We'll advise case-by-case.

Samir (Eng): For IT shipping: can devices go to Austin address?

Riley (People Ops): IT will ship after case approval and an IT ticket linking the case number. If hardware is company property and will be used abroad, you'll need to confirm import/export rules; Legal will help if needed.

Tess (Finance): Payroll note: submit the travel window before the payroll cutoff (10 business days prior) so we can compute prorated stipend and withholdings correctly.

Riley (People Ops): We'll publish a one-pager "split-location guidance" and an addendum template for recurring patterns. Posting link here when ready. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
